capabilities: Show one table row per item of a chosen list property, with a Source link to the note
Sort rows by multiple columns with shift-click
Update the table live when properties change and embed it via base view embeds
Export the flat table to a Markdown note or CSV file (Pro)
disambiguation: Not a Markdown table formatter; it is a Bases view that expands list properties into one row per item.
extras: Freemium: free tier flattens up to 50 notes; Pro ($5/month or $15 via GitHub Sponsors) removes the limit and adds grouping, filtering and export. Pro sign-in uses the GitHub device flow with limited read:user scope and works offline up to 14 days. After updates the plugin opens a What's new tab promoting other NoteMods plugins and a Telegram chat; it sends no note data.
intentEvidence: The base selects notes; Flatten Table draws rows through the public Bases API.
motivation: Built to answer the Bases forum request for a Dataview FLATTEN-style solution (forum topic 105425).
problem: The core Bases table view gives one row per note, so a list of objects in a note's properties collapses into a single cell.

relations.evidence: Dataview has FLATTEN in its query language, and it does not need Bases.

requires.name: GitHub Sponsors sponsorship of theluckystrike for Pro features

summary: Bases view that shows one table row for each item of a list property, so one note can produce many rows.
